deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Riemann's fair-copy draft of the opening of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page has the title and the table of contents. This page has (a) the historical note on the work's origin, (b) §1 and (c) §2 of the Erste Abtheilung. The text matches the printed version closely.

(a) Historical note. Apart from §§26–27, the paper is an extract from Riemann's Göttingen lectures, Michaelis 1855 to Michaelis 1856. He found the results of §1–5, 9 and 12, with their preparatory lemmas, in autumn 1851 and early 1852. Other work then drew him away. He resumed around Easter 1855 and carried the work through §21 in the Easter and Michaelmas vacations. The rest was added around Michaelis 1856, with supplements inserted during the write-up. No mathematics here; it is a dating statement.

(b) §1. Setup.
- Let F(s,z) = 0 be irreducible, of degree n in s, with coefficients that are polynomials of degree m in z.
- For each z there are n values of s. They vary continuously with z except where they become infinite.
- The branching is represented by an n-sheeted surface T spread over the z-plane. On T, s is a single-valued function of position.
- T is regarded as closed (compactified). Over z = ∞ each of the n sheets gets a point, unless T branches there.
- Every rational function R(s,z) is single-valued on T, so it has the same branching as s. Riemann announces that the converse will be proved later: every single-valued meromorphic function on T is rational in s,z.
- Integrals ∫R(s,z)dz have continuations over the same part of T that differ only by additive constants (periods). This is because the integrand takes the same value at the same point of T.
- Such systems of 'gleichverzweigte' algebraic functions and their integrals are to be defined by their singularities via the Dirichlet principle, not by explicit formulas.

(c) §2. Order of a zero.
- Definition: f is infinitely small of first order at a point P of T if log f increases by 2πi under one positive circuit of a neighbourhood of P on which f is finite and nonzero.
- Consequence: if T winds μ times around P (branch point of order μ−1) and z(P) = a is finite, then (z−a)^{1/μ} vanishes to first order. If z(P) = ∞, then (1/z)^{1/μ} does. In modern terms these are the local uniformizing parameters.
- Convention: a zero or pole of order ν at a point is treated as ν coincident (or infinitely close) simple zeros or poles.

Check of the local-parameter claim (my verification). One circuit around P on T projects to μ circuits of z around a. So arg(z−a) grows by 2πμ, and log (z−a)^{1/μ} grows by 2πi.

At ∞, a positive circuit around P is clockwise in the z-plane, μ times. So log z changes by −2πiμ, log(1/z) by +2πiμ, and log (1/z)^{1/μ} by 2πi.
errors: No mathematical errors. The statements are definitional and correct.
Minor: 'wo sie nicht unendlich werden' tacitly also excludes branch points from 'stetig ändern' in the sense of single branches. This is standard and harmless.

results.what: Compact n-sheeted Riemann surface T of an irreducible algebraic equation F(s,z)=0; rational functions of (s,z) are single-valued on T; the converse is announced.
results.modern_name: Compact Riemann surface of an algebraic curve; the function field equals the meromorphic functions on it
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851 dissertation; 1857 Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen)

results.what: Abelian integrals are multivalued with additive constants (periods).
Order of vanishing defined by the winding of the logarithm; local parameter (z−a)^{1/μ}, resp. (1/z)^{1/μ}, at a branch point of ramification μ.
results.modern_name: Local uniformizing parameter / order of a zero (valuation)

results.what: Plan to define functions by their singularities via the Dirichlet principle.
results.modern_name: Existence theorem for meromorphic functions/differentials with prescribed singularities

results.what: Dating of the discoveries: §1–5, 9, 12 in autumn 1851 to early 1852; resumed Easter 1855; finished Michaelis 1856.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own note in the published paper

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript draft of the published opening (historical note, §1, §2) of Riemann's 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'. The content and wording essentially match the printed text, which is very well known as his.

checkable.asserts: From the preceding page: p(p+1)/2 period parameters minus (p-2)(p-3)/2 relations leaves 3p-3 free moduli.
If z−a = e^{iμt} (one circuit on T as t goes 0→2π), then log((z−a)^{1/μ}) increases by 2πi, so it is a first-order zero.
Near z=∞, one positive circuit on T means z=e^{-iμt}; then log((1/z)^{1/μ}) = iμt/μ grows by 2πi.

transcription_corrections: 'die in §. 1–5, 9 und 12 dargestellten[?]' is probably 'dargelegten' (as in print).

The clause after 'vorbereitenden Sätze' reads roughly 'welche später behufs der Vorlesungen ... [erweitert/ausgearbeitet] ... wie sie in dieser Abhandlung gegeben ist'. The print has 'mit Ausnahme der Lehre von der Transformation, welche später behufs der Vorlesungen ausgearbeitet ...'. Check the image.
'(wie §[?])' after 'Stellt man daher' is uncertain. The printed text has no section reference there; the manuscript seems to read '(nach ...)' or similar. The transcription marker is warranted.
'durch einen andern Gegenstand von dieser Untersuchung abgezogen' is consistent with the image. The print reads 'durch eine andere Untersuchung von diesem Gegenstande abgezogen'.
'n-blättrige[?] Fläche' is plausible. The print has 'n-fach über derselben liegende Fläche T'.
